newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire government says battle on for Bunia.
newsitem.headline: Zaire government says battle on for Bunia.

text.p: Zaire's new crisis government said on Friday that fighting was raging in the centre of the disputed eastern town of Bunia and that Zairean troops still controlled the airport.
It was the first official government declaration on the fighting around the strategic mining town near the Ugandan border. Rebels say they captured Bunia on Tuesday.
"Bunia is not totally fallen," government spokesman Koloni Longo told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"Our armed forces are still in the centre of town where violent confrontations are taking place. The airport is under the control of the Zairean army," he added.
He added that many civilians had been killed but did not specify whether Zairean soldiers had also suffered heavy casualties, as the rebels have claimed.

Relief sources in Kinshasa in contact with the town said the airport was still in the hands of the Zairean army on Friday morning but that since then the fighting had been heavy around the airstrip and that no planes had been able to land.
The same sources said at least 300 people had been killed in the fighting.
The government spokesman could not confirm reports of Ugandan involvement in the latest fighting but accused Zaire's neighbours of involvement in earlier fighting.

He did confirm reports of looting by uncontrolled elements of the Zairean army 300 km (200 miles) to the west in the town of Isiro, and said an inquiry had been set up to establish the nature of the troubles and whether there had been killings.
He said that in Bunia itself there had been serious problems between different units of the Zaire army but that loyal troops had pacified rebellious elements.
Koloni denied reports that the town of Walikale 100 km (66 miles) west of Goma next to the Masisi region had been taken by the rebels.
Bunia is on the threshold of vast gold and mineral resources in the Upper Zaire province, and was one of the few remaining airstrips in the east used by the army to bring in reinforcements.
It is also at the head of one of the few passable roads in the region west to the town of Kisangani, in the heart of the jungle, and which the rebels have threatened to target.
Rebels say they captured Bunia the day the new government was appointed in the capital Kinshasa to confront the crisis in the east.
